long_biography.plain_text:
Shirley Temple began dance lessons at three and entered films the following year. Bright Eyes made her an international star, and at six she received a special Juvenile Academy Award. As Hollywood's leading child box-office attraction, she combined acting, singing and dancing with a licensing business that placed her image on dolls, clothing and household goods.

Temple left film at 22 after more than 40 screen appearances. Her mother had launched and closely managed the childhood career, while her father controlled finances that preserved only a small fraction of her earnings. She later built a distinct public-service career, serving as ambassador to Ghana, Chief of Protocol of the United States and ambassador to Czechoslovakia.
